thread:
support-jen: Customer reporting sudden 502/timeout spike to hosted inference in eu-west1 since 09:12 UTC. They say requests hang during TLS handshake, only for some clients behind AS 39523. :rotating_light:

mike: Any repro steps or packet traces from the customer?

support-jen: They provided a short cURL + tcpdump. cURL shows a reset during TLS read:
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate
* Rebuilt URL to: https://api.redwood.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate/
* Connected to api.redwood.redwood-inference.com (203.0.113.45) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.3 (IN), TLS unknown, Cipher is (none)
* SSL connection reset by peer
curl: (56) OpenSSL SSL_read: Connection reset by peer, errno 104
```
They also included tcpdump snippets showing lots of ICMP "Fragmentation needed" and some AAAA answers from their resolver.

hana: Hm — that pattern smells like PMTU + IPv6 dual-stack: resolver returns AAAA, client attempts IPv6 path, ClientHello (TLSv1.3) is large (>1200 bytes) and gets fragmented; middlebox drops fragments or blocks ICMP, causing handshake stall/resets.

support-jen: Uploaded full pcap at https://files.redwood.dev/escalations/2967894321.pcap (trimmed) — customer confirms the issue only happens when their resolver prefers AAAA.

mike: Quick checks for triage: 1) confirm edge sees AAAA answer for that client IP, 2) check for ICMP type 3 code 4 (frag needed) from path, 3) look at MSS/DF flags in packets. If confirmed, mitigation = force v4 for that ASN or ask customer to switch to IPv4 resolver (1.1.1.1) temporarily.

sara: I'll write a short runbook snippet: steps to detect PMTU-related TLS failures -> look for repeated SYN/ACK then client hello retransmits, ICMP need-frag, and CH length >1200. Workaround: reply with v4 A-only for affected prefixes at edge or enable MTU-safe TLS CH sizing for a canary subset.

eng-infra-bot: escalation created: #inc-2026-1439 (priority=P2) — assigned to eng-infra. Pinging @eng-infra.

mike: Assigning to hana to lead network triage. Hana, can you confirm if we should BGP-blackhole or apply an A-only override for that ASN as a short-term fix?

hana: Will triage. Plan: capture dual-stack pcap at edge, confirm ICMP need-frag, coordinate with network team for an A-only prefix override for the ASN, and push a temporary edge config to prefer IPv4 for requests from that client ASN. Targeting EOD for mitigation and follow-up with customer. :thumbsup:
